Article Title: Gen Z outreach: PM Modi asks ministers to shore up presence on Insta
Article Text:
PM Modi on video

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the response to his midnight post on Instagram Thursday, which got 305 million views, PM Modi Friday returned to the social media platform. "Thank you, friends. I had an opportunity to connect with you late last night. The way you responded to my video post and gave constructive suggestions, thanks to everybody. Your love will continue and our bond will strengthen," the PM said, reports Dipak Dash.His remarks reflected satisfaction, with officials calling it a "successful connect" with Gen Z, who have been wooed by CJP and other opponents. Within minutes, Friday's video had garnered 9.3 million views.This came barely hours after PM urged his Cabinet colleagues to use more of Instagram, saying it will help them stay connected with the youth. He was interacting with them after the Cabinet meeting on Friday. Official sources said PM's choice of Instagram to announce govt's decision to toughen the anti-paper leak law earned him around 1 million new followers.Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked ministers how many of them were actively using social media platforms such as Instagram.He said the platform has been popular with large sections of youth and emphasised using the social networking site to connect with them.PM Modi has been using Instagram since 2014.His advice comes amid a growing sense that BJP, which successfully leveraged mass use of WhatsApp to steal a march over its rivals, runs the risk of ceding the advantage in reaching out to Gen Z, which is not as enamoured of the messaging platform and is more comfortable with the photo & short form video service.PM Modi, a tech enthusiast, has repeatedly urged his ministers to hold interactive sessions with youth on this platform. He has said govt as well as BJP should more active on social media. Chairing the council of ministers meeting in Jan 2023, he had stressed that social media had emerged as the main source of information for large sections of the youth and its growing allure needed to be harnessed.
Article Summary: Pm modi on video posted on instagram: "thank you, friends. I had an opportunity to connect with you late last night" within minutes, friday's video had garnered 9.3 million views. This came barely hours after pm urged his cabinet colleagues to use instagram.

Article Title: Why the world is coming to India for medical treatment — and not just because it is cheaper
Article Text:
People coming from various countries to India for cardio surgeries, IVF treatment, dental care, etc.

What is medical tourism?

Government focus

India ranks 10th on medical tourism index

Why patients are choosing India

Beyond affordability

Areas for improvement

The next phase of growth

A hip replacement in Vadodara. A dental procedure in Chennai. An IVF treatment in Delhi. Every year, hundreds of thousands of patients travel to India not for its monuments or beaches, but for its medical care.What was once driven largely by patients from neighbouring countries seeking affordable treatment has evolved into a broader medical travel ecosystem.Industry estimates cited by the Economic Survey 2025–26 and the government project India's medical tourism market to grow from around $8.7 billion in 2025 to $16.2 billion by 2030. Over the same period, the global Medical Value Travel market is projected to expand from $115.6 billion in 2022 to $286.1 billion by 2030. Additionally, India's broader hospital and healthcare delivery market is expected to grow at 10–12 per cent annually, reaching nearly Rs 12 trillion by FY30, with private hospital chains projected to expand capacity from around 70,000 beds to more than 108,000 by 2030.India ranks 10th among the world's 46 medical tourism destinations, according to the Medical Tourism Index 2020–21.Let’s dive deep into the medical world and see how much potential India offers to tourists.Medical tourism refers to patients travelling outside their home country to seek planned medical treatment. While lower treatment costs remain a major factor, patients also consider waiting times, access to specialists, quality of care, language support and post-treatment follow-up when choosing a destinationFor India, the demand spans a wide range of services, from cardiac surgery and joint replacements to cancer treatment, fertility care, organ transplants, dental treatment, cosmetic procedures and neurological interventions.Improvements in digital consultations and easier access to treatment information have also made it simpler for patients to compare hospitals and plan their care before travelling.The Union Budget 2026–27 has proposed the development of five Regional Medical Hubs in partnership with state governments and the private sector. These hubs will combine medical, educational and research facilities, along with AYUSH centres and dedicated Medical Value Tourism facilitation centres.To further facilitate such travel, India offers e-Medical Visa and e-Medical Attendant Visa facilities, which have been extended to nationals of 172 countries, along with newer e-AYUSH Visa categories for those seeking traditional Indian systems of medicine. The government is also upgrading its Heal in India (Medical Value Travel) portal into a single platform for hospital discovery, treatment planning, bookings, payments and post-operative care, while airport concierge services have been proposed to assist international patients on arrival.Notably, according to government data, India has 69,364 hospitals; including 43,486 private and 25,778 public facilities, along with around 1.2 million registered doctors and more than 1,299 NABH-accredited hospitals as of 2026. Several hospitals are also accredited by the Joint Commission International (JCI), with most located in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad.For patients who make the journey, affordability is often only part of the story.India recorded 507,244 foreign arrivals for medical treatment in 2025, accounting for about 5.5 per cent of total foreign tourist arrivals that year; as compared to about 112,000 in 2009. Bangladesh was the largest source market with 3,25,127 arrivals, followed by Iraq (30,989), Uzbekistan (13,699), Somalia (11,506), Turkmenistan (10,231), Oman (9,738) and Kenya (9,357).People have given various reasons for choosing India.American traveller Charlie Evans, who sought treatment for seasonal flu and an ear complaint at a hospital in Rishikesh, said he was initially hesitant about seeking medical care in a foreign country. However, he described being greeted by English-speaking staff, facing almost no waiting time and receiving treatment using equipment comparable to what he had seen in the United States.Evans said his consultation, medication and treatment cost around $10–20, compared with an estimated $150 for a similar visit in the US. "I got better care in Rishikesh, faster and cheaper, than I've ever gotten at home," he said.Beyond the lower cost, Evans said what stood out was the professionalism of the medical staff. "The doctor who treated me could have easily been practising in the US," he said, adding that healthcare in India felt to him less like a profit-driven system and more focused on patient care.The experience reflects a broader trend, where patients increasingly weigh convenience and quality alongside costs.American content creator Kristen Fischer, who lives in India, has also praised the country's healthcare system. While she believes the US offers a better overall hospital experience, she said she prefers India's healthcare system because it is "simple, affordable, fast" and offers "quality treatment.""One thing I love about Indian healthcare is that you pay before treatment. Then after you leave the hospital you never have to pay or worry about anything else again," Fischer said, contrasting it with the US, where patients can receive bills "for months after" treatment. She also argued that India's upfront pricing makes costs more transparent, unlike in the US where insurance often shields patients from the true cost of treatment, contributing to higher healthcare expenses."The cost is clearly defined before treatment. This allows people to shop around for a good deal according to their budget," she said.Fischer, in her series of social media posts, has also highlighted the accessibility of healthcare in India, saying patients can often see a doctor the same day without an appointment, unlike in the US where consultations can take weeks. She has described Indian doctors as "way less rushed and more attentive to your needs" and recounted receiving treatment for a thumb injury at a Delhi hospital in about 45 minutes for just Rs 50.The cost advantage is evident even for routine procedures too. Sej, who lives in Utrecht in the Netherlands, said she schedules her dental appointments around her trips to India. "A 30-minute teeth cleaning costs around 185 euros near where I live. In Lucknow, I pay about Rs 3,000 for the same treatment," she said.Aditya Oza, CEO of CureMeAbroad, which connects international patients with accredited hospitals, said India is beginning to attract patients who once favoured destinations such as Turkey and Thailand.He cited a case where two people who had earlier travelled to Turkey for treatment but chose India for their latest procedure. "Patients who've already been through this once, who know what to look for, are increasingly landing on India specifically. The accreditation is there, the specialist experience is there, and the cost gap is often the widest of any destination," he said."What's changed is that patients now have a way to verify all of that upfront instead of guessing."Hospital executives believe India's competitiveness will increasingly depend on the overall patient experience rather than just costs.Dr Sonia Lal Gupta, joint managing director of Metro Group of Hospitals, said accreditation, transparent clinical outcomes and accountability remain important differentiators."What we haven't fully built yet is the trust and the experience around that care, and that is where the real opportunity lies," she said.She added that support should extend beyond the hospital stay, covering everything from the first enquiry and medical visa assistance to treatment, recovery and follow-up consultations after patients return home.Meanwhile, Dr Sharan Shivaraj Patil, founder and chairman of SPARSH Group of Hospitals, said providers are investing in dedicated international patient services to make treatment easier from the first inquiry through recovery. It includes pre-arrival teleconsultations, medical visa assistance, transparent treatment plans with cost estimates, airport transfers, accommodation support, language interpretation, culturally appropriate meals and post-treatment follow-up. "As the expectations of international patients continue to evolve, the focus remains on delivering world-class clinical outcomes complemented by personalised, culturally sensitive and compassionate care," he added.Meanwhile, UK content creator Reuben Charles, who is currently in Guwahati, said he was impressed by the convenience and professionalism of his healthcare experience in India after using an at-home medical service to get some blood tests. He said the healthcare professional who attended to him was knowledgeable, spoke fluent English and took the time to explain the procedure in detail."The service was great. It was very, very quick as well. It came right to my house," Charles said.He believes India's combination of quality, accessibility and convenience makes it an attractive destination for medical tourism, particularly for international patients who can afford private healthcareBritish traveller Jenny Mowbray, who spent five months in Kochi, also said India's healthcare system stood out for its speed, affordability and flexibility. Unable to easily access a second neurological opinion through the UK's public health system, she chose to undergo consultations and diagnostic tests in India."For me, the biggest attraction is the combination of accessibility, speed, quality, cost and choice," she said, highlighting the specialists' consult within a day, complete MRI scans and blood tests almost immediately and receiving results within hours.While describing her overall experience as "efficient, patient-centred and highly accessible," Mowbray said better access to verified information on hospitals, specialties and treatment costs could make India's medical tourism ecosystem even more attractive for international patients.Recounting her experience she said, " Before coming to India, I had already used healthcare services in Malaysia, Sri Lanka and Tunisia for a range of issues including my neurological concerns, gynaecological care and knee cartilage damage. During my five-month stay in Kochi, I wanted to have a mole checked and also revisit my neurological symptoms for peace of mind. "I was able to make appointments with both a dermatologist and a neurologist for the very next day.The dermatology consultation was extremely thorough," she added.Sharing another perspective, Jai Prakash, founder of Health Voyage Global, a medical tourism consultancy, said patients often come to India after struggling to get the right diagnosis. "Many patients believe they can receive the right diagnosis and treatment in India at a fraction of the cost they would pay elsewhere," he said. "Indian doctors are exposed to advanced medical equipment and global treatment protocols, allowing them to offer high-quality care with shorter treatment timelines and lower overall costs,” he added.Not every patient travels to India purely for lower costs or better hospitals. For some, crossing borders also offers privacy. A Delhi resident recounted how her neighbour had travelled alone to India from Nepal for IVF treatment because she faced social stigma and family pressure back home over fertility issues. Seeking treatment away from her community allowed her to undergo the procedure without the scrutiny and judgement.Despite rising patient numbers, hospitals say access to care remains uneven across the country.Dr Bharat S Mody, chairman of Welcare Hospital in Vadodara, said India attracts a steady stream of patients from neighbouring countries such as Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan, as well as from Africa and parts of Central Asia. However, he believes the country has yet to realise its full potential in attracting patients from Europe, the US and other developed markets.Mody said international patients are drawn by India's competitive pricing and medical expertise, but most treatment remains concentrated in metro cities, even though tier-2 centres can offer comparable quality at lower costs.Apart from this, he emphasised the medical visa process remains another hurdle for overseas patients."Our experience has also been that the government portal which issues the medical visa is not user-friendly," he said, adding that it "frustrates a potential patient wanting to come to India for medical treatment."He cited the example of Marco Bellaro, an Italian living in Indonesia, who travelled to Vadodara for a total hip replacement after finding the hospital online. Although Bellaro initially had concerns about hygiene standards and hospital infrastructure, Mody said those were addressed during consultations. The surgery was successful, but the medical visa process proved cumbersome, reiterating that simpler visa procedures and stronger global branding could help India attract more overseas patientsDr Alok Khullar, Group CEO of RJ Corp Healthcare, also emphasised on simplifying medical visa procedures, increasing the number of internationally accredited hospitals, improving coordination between airports and hospitals, and expanding multilingual support remain key priorities."Greater transparency around treatment costs and clinical outcomes will further strengthen confidence among patients and their families," he said.Patients, too, gave suggestions to fill out gaps beyond treatment itself. Charlie Evans, the American traveller, said a dedicated website or app for international patients, featuring hospital rankings, verified patient reviews and guidance on where to seek treatment for specific conditions, would make it easier for foreigners to navigate India's healthcare system with confidence.Adarsh Yadav, founder of healthcare companion platform CARESY, also emphasised on holistic services and care, saying India already has the clinical expertise to compete globally but must also focus on the patient journey. "If we can combine this with a smoother and more reassuring patient experience, India can become an even stronger destination for medical travellers," he said.India already has the ingredients - a large healthcare network, skilled medical professionals and a growing international patient base. As demand for cross-border healthcare grows globally, industry stakeholders believe India has the potential to attract even more.However, realising that opportunity, will require more than competitive treatment costs. The next phase of growth will depend on how effectively hospitals, governments, airlines, hotels, insurers and digital platforms work together to create a seamless patient journey.
Article Summary: Medical tourism refers to patients travelling outside their home country to seek planned medical treatment. India recorded 507,244 foreign arrivals for medical treatment in 2025, accounting for about 5.5 per cent of total foreign tourist arrivals. Bangladesh was the largest source market with 3,25,127 arrivals.

Article Title: SC bans posting court clips on social media
Article Text:
Apex court said any online use of audiovisual excerpts from hearings must have the approval of SC or HC.

Lawyers misusing court clips to lure clients, SC told

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Friday barred the uploading, sharing and circulation of video clips from live-streamed court proceedings on social media and digital platforms, after finding that edited clips with biased commentary were flooding social media. Apex court said any online use of audiovisual excerpts from hearings must have the approval of SC or HC.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the interim order after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for journalist PIL petitioner Harshita Grover, said some of these clips circulating on social media are edited with a devious mind and that a mischievous narrative is superimposed to project a negative image of the judiciary.Backing the PIL and a regulatory mechanism, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said use of AI has led to a manifold rise in spread of motivated narratives on social media, and could become a tool to malign judiciary's image.SC sought responses from govt, HCs and social media platforms - YouTube, X, WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram - in two weeks."As an interim measure, no excerpts from live-streamed judicial proceedings will be posted, transmitted, stored, hosted or circulated on any social media or digital platforms without prior permission of SC secretary general or registrars general of jurisdictional HCs," the bench said.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, who is also president of Supreme Court Bar Association, flagged advocates posting clips of court proceedings involving them on social media apparently to boost popularity and attract clients.SC has sought a response from Bar Council of India as Advocates Act bars lawyers from advertising or soliciting clients directly or indirectly.Apart from social media activity, many law firms now have engaged PR professionals who approach journalists to incorporate quotes from them in news articles.The misuse of court clips on social media was such that the CJI-led bench considered suspending the live streaming of judicial hearings, which began during the Covid lockdown."If the digital data generated from the court hearings after going public becomes difficult to regulate, we will consider restricting live-streaming of court proceedings, as we do not want it to become a 24x7 entertainment channel. It is trivialising the judiciary," the bench said.When the bench said availability of links to live proceedings could be restricted only to advocates and litigants on demand, Singh said live streaming should not be stopped as it gives transparency to judicial proceedings.The petitioner said fair reporting of judicial proceedings was protected under the right to free speech under Article 19, and the protection did not extend to mischievous and denigrating contents that interfere with the administration of justice, spread misinformation or subject judicial institutions to organised vilification campaigns."Misleading thumbnails, clickbait headlines, provocative commentary, and edited courtroom clips encourage sensationalism rather than accurate reporting. These practices distort public understanding of judicial proceedings and erode confidence in the justice delivery system," Harshita Grover said.
Article Summary: Apex court said any online use of audiovisual excerpts from hearings must have the approval of sc or hc. Solicitor general tushar mehta said use of ai has led to a rise in spread of motivated narratives on social media.

Article Title: 4.1cr kids obese, ICMR seeks tighter curbs
Article Text:
Nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese

NEW DELHI: With World Obesity Atlas 2026 saying nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese, Indian Council of Medical Research unveiled a roadmap this week to halt the trend.Key proposals include front-of-pack nutrition labelling, restrictions on market-ing of unhealthy foods to chi-ldren, healthier school food environments, improved nutrition literacy, and fiscal measures such as taxes on foods high in fat, salt and sugar (HFSS).It also calls for stricter enforcement of existing FSSAI regulations that prohibit sale and advertising of foods high in saturated fat, trans fat, added sugar and sodium within school campuses and within 50m of their gates. The document recommends routine inspections, stronger monitoring and greater accountability to improve compliance.A pilot assessment in UP private schools found ultra-processed snacks and sugary drinks were widely available in school canteens, nutrition services were limited, and existing nutrition policies were poorly implemented. The report says the absence of a legally operational definition of HFSS foods has weakened enforcement of regulations.The report warns India could account for more than 11% of the global childhood obesity burden by 2030 if current trends continue. It also estimates that unhealthy diets account for 56.4% of the country's disease burden, with easy access to HFSS foods, aggressive marketing and poor nutrition literacy driving obesity.The roadmap, launched by Niti Aayog member (health) M Srinivas under the ICMR-NIN-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' initiative, brings together 10 policy briefs developed over nearly three years of research.
Article Summary: World obesity atlas 2026 says nearly 4.1 crore indian children are already overweight or obese. Indian council of medical research unveiled a roadmap this week to halt the trend. Key proposals include front-of-pack nutrition labelling, restrictions on market-ing of unhealthy foods.

Article Title: Government pushes competition in power distribution
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: Union power ministry’s consultative committee met on Thursday to discuss a consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing that would allow multiple electricity suppliers to use the same distribution network.The proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition, reduce infrastructure duplication and give consumers the freedom to choose their electricity provider.The draft National Electricity Policy-2026, which is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon, has also underlined the need to phase out monopoly in electricity distribution and introduce competition by allowing multiple players.According to officials, the existing legal framework permits more than one distribution licensee in the same area, but requires each of them to establish its own distribution network. This results in duplication of infrastructure, higher capital expenditure, discourages fresh investment and leads to “inefficient utilisation of resources”.Mumbai is the only city where consumers have exercised supplier choice for several years, while the distribution network is developed in a coordinated manner under the supervision of the state electricity regulatory commission.Emphasising the consumer-centric nature of the reform, Union power minister Manohar Lal said consumers would have the freedom to choose their electricity supplier, similar to the choices available today in sectors such as telecom and aviation. "Increased competition is expected to encourage better consumer service, improved reliability, greater innovation and operational efficiency, while ensuring optimal utilisation of existing infrastructure and avoiding unnecessary expenditure," the minister said at the meeting.Power ministry, in a statement, said members of Parliament who are part of the consultative committee offered valuable suggestions on the proposed framework. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks."New distribution licensees will be able to use the existing network by paying regulated wheeling charges, while retaining the option to develop their own network wherever permitted by the concerned state electricity regulatory commission," govt said in the statement.
Article Summary: Proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition and reduce infrastructure duplication. Draft national electricity policy-2026 is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks.

Article Title: NTA terminates 47 officials, begins specialist-led rebuild
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: The National Testing Agency has terminated 47 officials and begun rebuilding its workforce with specialist leadership in cybersecurity, forensic investigation, test-centre operations and assessment research, government sources said on Friday.Some of those terminated will also face legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies. More measures are expected as responsibility is fixed for failures in national entrance examinations.The first phase includes four General Manager appointments and 16 Young Professionals through UPSC’s PRATIBHA Setu portal. Recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting on Saturday, July 25, ministry sources said.The crackdown follows the NEET-UG paper leak, which forced nearly 20 lakh candidates to take the examination again on June 21 after the May 3 test was cancelled. Sources stressed that the 47 personnel had been terminated, not merely transferred or marked for removal. Their names, ranks and alleged roles were not disclosed. Cases indicating criminal wrongdoing will be referred to the appropriate agencies, while departmental and legal proceedings will follow separately.The four General Managers will be appointed on three-year contracts.The assessment and psychometrics head will oversee question banks, normalisation, equating and calibration, and pilots on computer-adaptive testing and AI-assisted assessment.The test-centre operations head will supervise NTA ’s network across more than 500 cities and select overseas centres, including empanelment, capacity, accessibility, amenities, examination-day operations and coordination with administrations.The information-security head will serve as Chief Information Security Officer, responsible for systems, networks, applications, candidate data, a round-the-clock Security Operations Centre and compliance with data-protection, information-technology and CERT-In requirements.The vigilance, investigation and forensics head will lead malpractice inquiries, build in-house digital-forensics capability and coordinate with the CBI, Intelligence Bureau, Enforcement Directorate, state police and cybercrime units under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.NTA will also engage 16 Young Professionals through PRATIBHA Setu — Professional Resource And Talent Integration Bridge for Hiring Aspirants — for the first time. The platform gives verified employers access to willing candidates who cleared stages of UPSC examinations but were not recommended in the final merit list.Twelve positions will be in academic research, two in legal research and two in finance and accounts. Appointments will initially be for 24 months, extendable to 36 months based on performance.The changes seek to reduce NTA’s dependence on temporary manpower. It has 39 sanctioned permanent posts, all on deputation, but only 24 are filled, against 73 contractual personnel and 124 outsourced workers.Further hiring will follow across 10 functional verticals recommended by the Radhakrishnan committee. NTA has also initiated fresh empanelment of subject experts and translators.The overhaul will accompany changes to examination delivery. NEET-UG will shift from OMR-based testing to computer-based testing from 2027, bringing it closer to JEE Main and CUET. The move should reduce physical movement of papers, enable multiple question sets and create a digital trail, but will require secure centres, stronger cybersecurity and safeguards against technical failures.The government is also reviewing outsourcing in registration, centre management, technology services and handling of confidential material. The new model will define responsibility, strengthen audits and background checks, reduce agencies handling sensitive information and impose tougher penalties for security failures.Sources said the reset would combine accountability for past lapses with safeguards against future leaks and malpractice.
Article Summary: The first phase includes four general manager appointments and 16 young professionals through upsc’s pratibha setu portal. Recruitment will be overseen by the k radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting on saturday, july 25.

Article Title: 'Substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements': Government directs GitHub to take down Bluetooth-based Bitchat app
Article Text:
The app allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages

Govt flags anonymous, offline messaging as security risk

Notice follows use of offline messaging apps during Delhi protests

NEW DELHI: The Union government's cybercrime coordination centre has directed Microsoft-owned GitHub to remove Bitchat, a Bluetooth-based messaging application developed by former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey, citing concerns that it could be misused by terrorists, organised crime groups and anti-national elements to evade lawful surveillance.The notice comes after authorities observed several participants in the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar using Bluetooth-based messaging applications after temporary internet restrictions were imposed around the protest site.Sharing a copy of the July 23 notice on X on Friday, Dorsey claimed, "The Government of India does not like technologies like Bitchat and wants it taken down."The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), which functions under the Union home ministry, has not immediately responded to queries regarding the notice, according to news agency PTI.In its notice to GitHub, I4C said Bitchat is among a number of applications capable of enabling decentralised peer-to-peer messaging over Bluetooth mesh networks without relying on mobile networks, internet connectivity or centralised servers.According to the notice, the application allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages."The technical architecture of the application significantly impedes lawful interception, attribution and investigation by law enforcement agencies," the notice said.The agency argued that because messages are transmitted directly between nearby devices through a decentralised mesh network, such platforms could be used to evade lawful surveillance, facilitate anonymous coordination and bypass internet restrictions imposed during situations involving public disorder, riots, terrorism, organised crime or internet shutdowns."Intelligence inputs indicate that such decentralised communication platforms are capable of being exploited for coordinating unlawful assemblies, violent protests, dissemination of misinformation, radicalisation, criminal conspiracies, and other activities prejudicial to the sovereignty and integrity of India, defence of India, security of the State, public order, and for facilitating the commission of cognizable offences," the notice stated.It further said the absence of a centralised service provider limits the ability of law enforcement agencies to obtain subscriber information, communication records or timely assistance during investigations."The application's design, which enables communication even during network restrictions, creates a substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements, terrorist organisations, organised criminal groups, and cybercriminals seeking to evade lawful detection and continue communication despite legally imposed restrictions," the notice added.I4C has alleged that the app violates Sections 43, 84B and 84C of the Information Technology Act, along with Section 61 read with Sections 196 and 197 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.The CJP has been leading protests over the NEET paper leak and is demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Earlier on Friday, representatives of the CJP held a nearly two-hour meeting with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.Following the meeting, the outfit reiterated that Pradhan's resignation remained a "non-negotiable" demand and also sought Rs 1 crore compensation for families of students who died by suicide after the cancellation of the NEET examination, along with the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters.Union health minister JP Nadda said the CJP delegation had presented three key demands and five suggestions for examination reforms, and the government would respond after internal discussions.Another round of talks between the two sides is scheduled for Saturday.
Article Summary: Bitchat app allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages. Indian cybercrime coordination centre (i4c), which functions under the union home ministry, has not immediately responded to queries regarding the notice.

Article Title: Scientists discovered an underwater city of 60-million fish nests beneath Antarctica's ice shelf
Article Text:
Image: AI Generated

A robot explored beneath Antarctica's ice shelf and confirmed a hidden underwater metropolis

Why these transparent icefish build millions of nests beneath the Antarctic ice

A slightly warmer pocket of ocean makes this extraordinary nursery possible

Why Weddell seals turn this breeding ground into a seasonal hunting ground

Why scientists believe the colony deserves stronger protection

Hidden beneath hundreds of metres of Antarctic ice lies one of the planet's most extraordinary wildlife spectacles. After drilling through the Filchner Ice Shelf, scientists deployed an autonomous underwater robot into the dark waters below, where it revealed what can only be described as an underwater city, a sprawling breeding colony covering an area roughly the size of Orlando, Florida. Spread across the seafloor were an estimated 60 million nests, each carefully built and guarded by transparent, antifreeze-blooded Antarctic icefish. Yet this remarkable nursery is also the setting for a relentless struggle for survival, as hungry Weddell seals transform the breeding season into a deadly feeding ground. The discovery is reshaping scientists' understanding of Antarctica's hidden ecosystems and their importance to the Southern Ocean. It also highlights how much of Antarctica's underwater world remains unexplored, with future expeditions likely to uncover even more hidden ecosystems beneath the continent's vast ice shelves. Scientists say the colony's stability over multiple years is itself a striking finding, since it suggests this hidden ecosystem has quietly persisted at massive scale for far longer than researchers previously had any reason to suspect.The vast breeding colony lies beneath the Filchner Ice Shelf in the southern Weddell Sea, one of the most remote and inaccessible marine environments on Earth.The colony was first identified during a 2021 expedition led by Dr Autun Purser of the Alfred Wegener Institute (AWI), Helmholtz Centre for Polar and Marine Research , using the Ocean Floor Observation and Bathymetry System (OFOBS). The team's findings revealed an astonishing concentration of nests extending across approximately 240 square kilometres, an area comparable to the size of Orlando. The researchers estimated that the site contains around 60 million active nests, making it the largest fish breeding colony ever discovered.More recently, AWI scientists returned with LASSIE (Low-Altitude Survey System for Icefish), an autonomous underwater vehicle specifically designed to monitor the colony beneath the ice shelf. Operating continuously for 48 hours, LASSIE confirmed that both the colony's size and nesting density have remained remarkably stable since the original discovery, providing researchers with the first long-term baseline for monitoring this unique ecosystem.The colony belongs to the blackfin icefish (Neopagetopsis ionah), one of Antarctica's most unusual fish species. Icefish are famous for lacking haemoglobin, the red protein that carries oxygen in the blood of almost every other vertebrate. As a result, their blood appears almost transparent. They also produce specialised antifreeze glycoproteins that prevent ice crystals from forming inside their bodies, allowing them to survive in seawater that remains below the normal freezing point of fresh water. These remarkable adaptations have enabled the species to thrive in one of the planet's coldest and most extreme marine environments.Each nest is a circular depression measuring roughly 75 centimetres in diameter, cleared of fine sediment to expose small stones that help protect the eggs. Researchers found that a typical nest contains around 1,700 eggs, while an adult fish, usually the male, stands guard until they hatch. Across the colony, nests occur at an average density of about 0.26 nests per square metre, creating an immense network of breeding sites stretching as far as the cameras could see. The study was led by Dr Autun Purser and an international team of researchers from the Alfred Wegener Institute, the University of Bremen, the Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology, the University of Basel and other institutions.aScientists discovered that the breeding colony exists in a remarkably specific part of the seafloor, revealing an unexpected hotspot for Antarctic marine reproduction.Measurements showed that modified Warm Deep Water flowing through the Filchner Trough keeps the seabed beneath the colony up to 2°C warmer than surrounding bottom waters. Although still close to freezing, this subtle temperature difference appears sufficient to create ideal breeding conditions for the icefish.The researchers believe this narrow band of relatively warmer water explains why millions of fish concentrate their nests in one location rather than spreading across the Antarctic seafloor. Without these favourable oceanographic conditions, such an enormous breeding aggregation would probably not exist. The finding also highlights how small environmental differences can shape the distribution and reproductive success of entire marine populations over vast areas.The underwater city does not remain peaceful for long.Using satellite tracking data collected over many years, researchers found that Weddell seals (Leptonychotes weddellii) repeatedly travel to the breeding colony during the nesting season. The dense concentration of adult fish provides an abundant food source, making the area one of the seals' most important feeding grounds.Scientists also documented numerous fish carcasses scattered throughout the colony, demonstrating that while millions of icefish gather to reproduce, many become prey before the breeding season ends. This intense predation helps transfer enormous amounts of energy through the Antarctic food web, supporting predators while recycling nutrients back into the surrounding ecosystem.Rather than representing ecological failure, the seasonal "massacre" is a natural process that links one of Earth's largest fish nurseries with the broader Southern Ocean ecosystem.The discovery has transformed scientific understanding of Antarctic marine ecosystems.According to Dr Autun Purser and colleagues, the breeding colony represents not only the largest known fish nesting site on Earth but also one of Antarctica's most significant concentrations of marine biomass. Because millions of breeding fish gather in a single location each year, researchers argue that the area should receive enhanced conservation protection.The findings have already strengthened proposals for expanding Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) in the Weddell Sea. Long-term monitoring with autonomous systems such as LASSIE will also allow scientists to measure how climate change, ocean warming and shifting sea-ice conditions affect one of the planet's most extraordinary hidden ecosystems.Far beneath Antarctica's frozen surface, where sunlight never reaches and temperatures remain near freezing, an underwater city continues to thrive, its millions of carefully guarded nests reminding scientists that some of Earth's greatest natural wonders remain hidden beneath the ice.
Article Summary: An underwater robot explored beneath antarctica's filchner ice shelf. It found a vast breeding colony of transparent, antifreeze-blooded icefish. The site contains around 60 million active nests, making it the largest fish breeding colony ever discovered. The breeding colony is the largest known fish nesting site on earth.

Article Title: Florida gets its first underwater research habitat in around 40 years, where scientists will soon live beneath the ocean
Article Text:
image AI generated

How DEEP installed the Vanguard underwater habitat in the Florida Keys

How the Vanguard underwater habitat will study human health beneath the ocean

How the Vanguard underwater habitat could transform human health research

Vanguard underwater habitat to advance coral research, medicine and astronaut training

A new underwater habitat has taken its place on the seabed off the Florida Keys, offering scientists something they have not had in US waters for decades: a permanent place to live and work beneath the ocean for days at a time. Ocean infrastructure company DEEP has installed its Vanguard pilot habitat at Tennessee Reef inside the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary. Positioned 17 metres (56 feet) below the surface, the structure is entering its final commissioning phase before hosting its first research crews. It is the first open-ocean subsea human habitat to be built, tested and deployed in the United States in around 40 years, marking a return to long-duration underwater research after a lengthy gap.The deployment required a carefully planned offshore operation. Engineers first secured a foundation on the seabed before attaching the cylindrical habitat and connecting it to a nearby surface support buoy. The completed system now rests on a sandy section of the reef at a depth suitable for saturation-style missions. According to Ocean Science and Technology, the habitat's living section stretches 10.7 metres in length and around 2.5 metres in diameter.Once certification work is complete, it will be able to accommodate four aquanauts for research expeditions lasting at least five days.Sea acceptance testing is currently underway ahead of classification by maritime assurance organisation DNV. DEEP will then begin training habitat support crews before the first operational missions commence. According to Ocean Science and Technology, Norman Smith, DEEP's Chief Technology Officer, the installation followed around 18 months of design, construction and testing.“Installing Vanguard at Tennessee Reef was a carefully choreographed marine operation with a lot of moving parts," Smith said, adding that successful deployment moves the company closer to enabling "a continuous human presence in the ocean" and expanding access for marine science, environmental monitoring and extreme-environment training.Although coral reefs and marine ecosystems will be among Vanguard's primary research targets, the habitat has another role that receives less public attention: studying the people living inside it.Reportedly, DEEP Director of Scientific Research, Dawn Kernagis, explained that underwater habitats create opportunities across three areas of science. Alongside marine research and testing life-support technologies, scientists can examine how the human body responds to prolonged exposure beneath the sea.According to Kernagis, underwater environments share several characteristics with other extreme settings such as spaceflight and high-altitude expeditions. "You're potentially breathing different gases, you're at different pressure exposures, and you see changes in how the body functions, from the molecular level to the cardiovascular and nervous system," she wrote. Those physiological changes allow researchers to understand how healthy people respond to unusual environmental stress before applying those findings to medicine on land.Scientists have investigated saturation divers for decades, but much of the available human research dates back many years. Advances in genetics, wearable monitoring, molecular biology and biomedical analysis now make it possible to observe biological responses with much greater precision than was previously achievable. As per reports, Kernagis said one of Vanguard's biggest advantages is that it functions as a laboratory rather than simply a place where divers sleep between missions.During earlier underwater projects, blood and tissue samples often had to be brought back to the surface before analysis. That introduced decompression-related changes, making it harder to separate the effects of living underwater from the effects of returning to normal atmospheric pressure. Processing biological samples while crews remain at depth could allow scientists to observe cellular and molecular responses in real time. She described that capability as potentially changing research across undersea medicine, immunology and human physiology.The work planned for Vanguard extends well beyond studying divers themselves. The habitat will support coral restoration projects, continuous reef monitoring, climate impact assessments, species surveys, ocean sensor testing and astronaut training. Scientists also expect to use the platform for educational broadcasts, allowing audiences to communicate live with crews working on the seabed.Human health research forms another part of that programme. Lessons from prolonged underwater missions could improve understanding of oxygen therapy, cardiovascular responses, immune function, sleep, nutrition, thermal regulation and continuous patient monitoring. Research into pressure exposure may also contribute to work involving hyperbaric medicine, wound healing and treatment for conditions such as carbon monoxide poisoning or gas embolism.Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary superintendent Eddie Kertis said subsea habitats have supported marine discoveries for decades and that the new installation creates additional opportunities for long-term scientific work while strengthening research infrastructure within the protected reef.
Article Summary: Vanguard underwater habitat has been installed on the seabed off the florida keys. It is the first open-ocean subsea human habitat to be built, tested and deployed in the united states in around 40 years. The habitat will support coral restoration projects, continuous reef monitoring, climate impact assessments, species surveys, ocean sensor testing and astronaut training.

Article Title: Vietnam moves to bar under-16s from posting, commenting on social media
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the idea of requiring social media accounts for children under 16 to be registered through a parent or guardian? Yes, it enhances safety No, it restricts freedom 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Vietnam is planning to require social media platforms to stop users under the age of 16 from posting content, commenting or reacting to posts, under a draft decree aimed at strengthening online protections for children, according to a document reviewed by Reuters.The proposed rules would require social media accounts belonging to children under 16 to be registered using the information of a parent or legal guardian, who would be responsible for supervising the content viewed by children and the amount of time they spend on the platforms.The draft decree also requires social media companies to use technical measures to identify child users and ensure that they receive age-appropriate content. Platforms would have to provide the highest level of privacy protection for child accounts and proactively detect, warn and block access to content related to violence, pornography, gambling, drugs, suicide and other harmful material."The primary objective is not to ban or excessively restrict children's access to social media, but rather to ensure that when children use social media services, they are placed in an age-appropriate environment and protected from inappropriate risks," deputy culture minister Phan Tam said on Thursday during a meeting to discuss the proposed rules.The proposal comes as governments across the world tighten regulations on children's use of social media amid growing concerns over online safety and the impact of harmful content on young users' mental health.Earlier this week, French lawmakers approved a ban on social media access for children under 15. Australia became the first country to impose such a ban, while several other countries are considering similar measures.The draft decree also proposes new restrictions on online gaming by minors. Game operators would be required to verify users' ages, register accounts of children under 16 through a parent or legal guardian, and limit users under 16 to a maximum of 60 minutes of gameplay per day across games offered by the same company.The draft decree has not yet been finalised and may be revised before it is formally adopted.
Article Summary: Vietnam is planning to require social media platforms to stop users under the age of 16 from posting content, commenting or reacting to posts. The draft decree is aimed at strengthening online protections for children, according to a document reviewed by reuters. Platforms would have to provide the highest level of privacy protection for child accounts.

Article Title: FBI, NSA and CISA issue urgent warning: Iranian hackers hit critical US infrastructure and safety systems
Article Text:
FBI, NSA and CISA issued a joint warning

‘Tampering with safety alarms and emergency shutdowns’



Read the updated warning by FBI, NSA and CISA

The authoring agencies urgently warn U.S. organizations of ongoing Iranian-affiliated cyber targeting of internet-connected operational technology (OT) devices, including programmable logic controllers (PLCs). These actions disrupted PLCs across several U.S. critical infrastructure sectors through malicious project file interactions and manipulation of data on human machine interface (HMI) and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) displays, resulting in operational disruption and financial loss.

Last Update Description

This update adds new guidance on detecting malicious changes in reusable code modules exploited within Rockwell Automation PLC programs. It also expands scope to include observed targeting of

Schneider Electric

, Siemens, and potentially other branded/manufactured PLCs, emphasizing the importance of restricting direct internet access and providing best practices for secure deployment.

Affected Products

Potentially all internet exposed PLCs, including Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and other branded/manufactured PLCs.

Key Actions

Install PLCs consistent with manufacturers' guidelines and security best practices.



Remove PLCs from direct internet exposure via secure gateway and firewall; work with IT/OT team members and/or integrators to perform this action.



Query available logs for the provided indicators of compromise (IOCs) and check available logs for suspicious traffic on the ports associated with OT devices, including 44818, 2222, 102, and 502, especially traffic originating from foreign hosting providers.



For Rockwell Automation devices, place the physical mode switch on the controller into run position. If you suspect your organization was targeted, including against other branded PLC devices, contact the authoring agencies and PLC manufacturer for guidance.



US federal cyber agencies have issued an urgent joint warning, claiming that Iranian state-backed hackers are actively breaching and tampering with industrial control systems at US water and energy providers. In an updated security advisory, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the National Security Agency (NSA), the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and the Department of Energy warned that “potentially all internet-exposed” industrial control systems across critical US infrastructure could be vulnerable to attack.According to federal investigators, the Iranian-backed hackers are targeting programmable logic controllers, which are the specialised digital computers that govern physical machinery, valves, and power switches across utility networks.As per the warning, by altering display data and programming logic, the attackers have forced systems into dangerous operational states without alerting human supervisors. CISA and partner agencies are calling on all critical infrastructure operators to immediately audit their operational technology, disconnect industrial control systems from the public internet, and enforce strict multi-factor authentication.
Article Summary: Fbi, nsa and cisa issued a joint warning about iranian-affiliated cyber targeting of internet-connected operational technology (ot) devices. These actions disrupted plcs across several u.s. critical infrastructure sectors through malicious project file interactions and manipulation of data.

Article Title: Microsoft is quietly replacing OpenAI and Anthropic models inside GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook, and CEO Satya Nadella just explained the plan
Article Text:
Satya Nadella says Microsoft is now routing tasks inside GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook to its own MAI models whenever they match or beat frontier alternatives from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Why Microsoft built its own AI models instead of leaning on OpenAI and Anthropic

What reinforcement learning environments mean for Microsoft's enterprise customers

Microsoft has started routing work inside its own products away from OpenAI and Anthropic, and towards models it built itself. Satya Nadella laid out the reasoning in a long post on X, describing a system where Microsoft's in-house MAI models take over tasks once handled by frontier models from its partners. GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook are already showing what he called promising early results. Copilot Chat and PowerPoint are next in line.The logic is cost. Nadella's framing is that software now has a real marginal cost for the first time, which makes the choice of model a business decision rather than a technical default. Frontier models stay in the mix for frontier problems. Everything else gets pushed to something cheaper that performs just as well. Microsoft says its MAI models already beat general-purpose frontier models on many use cases while burning a fraction of the tokens.The MAI family arrived on June 2, when Mustafa Suleyman announced seven new models spanning reasoning, coding, image, voice and transcription. The flagship reasoning model, MAI-Thinking-1, was trained from scratch on what Microsoft calls clean, traceable data—no distillation from other labs.MAI-Code-1-Flash runs 5 billion active parameters and is built specifically for GitHub Copilot and VS Code. Microsoft claims it is comparable to Haiku but cheaper.That cheapness is the entire point. Microsoft's tuned model for Excel matches GPT 5.4 while running up to 10 times more efficiently, according to the company. At Microsoft's scale, across hundreds of millions of Office seats, that gap compounds fast.The mechanism Nadella keeps returning to is the reinforcement learning environment, or RLE. Rather than train a model in isolation and then bolt it onto a product, Microsoft trains models inside the actual product harness, rewarding them for finishing the tasks customers care about. Suleyman calls these training gyms. Microsoft is selling the same capability to enterprises through Foundry under the name Frontier Tuning, letting companies build models on their own workflow data.Nadella was careful about one detail. Models from OpenAI and Anthropic remain part of the orchestration system inside Microsoft products. He also set a test for whether Microsoft is genuinely in control: evaluation scores should keep improving even if any single model is pulled out. Memory, context, tools and skills sit outside the model deliberately, so no one vendor holds the leverage.For Microsoft, which has poured billions into OpenAI, that is a notable position to stake out publicly. The company is describing a template it expects other software firms to copy—use the expensive model where it earns its keep, and route the rest somewhere cheaper you own.
Article Summary: Microsoft has started routing work inside its own products away from openai and anthropic. Satya nadella laid out the reasoning in a long post on x, describing a system where microsoft's in-house mai models take over tasks once handled by frontier models.

Article Title: How one of Chinese AI models that Sam Altman wants banned, saved world’s biggest AI models repository Hugging Face from disaster that his company is responsible for
Article Text:
OpenAI admits its models went rogue in Hugging Face hack

Hugging Face says it turned to a Chinese AI model to fight back

Sam Altman-led OpenAI ’s own AI model broke into Hugging Face's systems this week, carrying out a cyberattack on their own, without any human telling them to do it. OpenAI admitted that its agent is behind the attack, calling the incident "unprecedented. " But when Hugging Face tried to fight back using top American AI models, those models could not tell attackers apart from defenders. Hugging Face then turned to GLM 5.2, an open-source Chinese AI model, to study the attack and stop it. The irony is sharp: OpenAI executives have pushed for the US government to restrict access to open Chinese models like this one, yet it was exactly this kind of model that saved OpenAI's own victim.OpenAI said that its models were behind the attack on Hugging Face, an open-source AI and machine learning platform. The models involved were GPT-5.6 Sol, a cybersecurity-focused model that the ChatGPT-maker recently released, and a second, more powerful model that has not yet been released to the public. The company said that both models acted on their own and broke into Hugging Face's system without being ordered to.When Hugging Face tried to use proprietary US AI models to respond to the attack, those models could not tell an incident responder from an attacker. Hugging Face said it then turned to GLM 5.2, an open-source model from China's Z.ai lab, and ran it on its own infrastructure. The Chinese model helped analyze more than 17,000 footprints left behind by the attackers.According to experts, the American models struggled because of their own built-in safety guardrails, which are stricter and more expensive to work around than the open-source Chinese model. Hugging Face said in its incident report that companies should keep "a capable model you can run on your own infrastructure vetted and ready before an incident."The timing lines up with a bigger debate over Chinese AI modelsHugging Face published its incident report the same day Chinese startup Moonshot AI released its Kimi K3 model, which it calls the world's largest open-weight AI model. The release shook global markets. Shares of Chinese competitors Zhipu and MiniMax fell 28.4% and 15.6% in Hong Kong trading. Shares of Z.ai, the lab behind GLM 5.2, also dropped 28.4%.The debate over open Chinese models has been building for weeks. OpenAI's head of strategic futures, Dean W. Ball, had argued the US government should create regulatory pressure against these models, since they compete on price with American frontier labs. Ball later walked back the claim. Earlier this week, Axios reported that the Trump administration is considering banning Kimi K3 and similar Chinese models, though Politico reported the Department of Commerce is not expected to act on this soon.
Article Summary: Openai admits its models went rogue in hugging face hack this week. Hugging face says it turned to a chinese ai model to fight back. The irony is sharp: openai executives have pushed for the us government to restrict access to open chinese models.

Why Microsoft is testing free game streaming now

Microsoft has started testing an ad-supported version of Xbox Cloud Gaming, letting players stream games they already own without a Game Pass subscription. The test went live on Thursday, July 23, and it is open only to members of the Xbox Insider programme. In exchange for skipping the subscription fee, players watch a block of ads before the stream begins, then get a one-hour session with no interruptions in between.The ad block runs for roughly two minutes and plays before you join the streaming queue, according to reports citing Xbox sources. Once you are in, the game runs as normal—no mid-session breaks, no overlays. You do get countdown warnings at the 10-minute and five-minute marks so you can find a save point. Want to keep going after the hour? Watch another two-minute block and requeue.Only games you already own, plus free-to-play titles. Variety reported that the eligible list includes Forza Horizon 6 and 007 First Light on the owned side, and Call of Duty: Warzone, Genshin Impact and War Thunder on the free-to-play side. That is a narrower pool than the 1,800-odd titles Xbox Cloud Gaming supports overall.There is a reason this is landing now. Xbox console prices go up again on August 1—the Series X hits $799.99 and the 512GB Series S goes to $499.99—which is the third hike driven partly by the memory shortage.Microsoft has also announced 3,200 layoffs across its games group and is looking to offload four studios. Cloud streaming on a device you already own is a cheaper on-ramp, and Microsoft is openly pitching it at markets where consoles are expensive or hard to find.Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball framed the goal as giving players more affordable options and learning from how they use it. Microsoft published five principles for ads across Xbox, including a promise not to interrupt gameplay. Game Pass subscribers, who pay from $9.99 a month, keep ad-free streaming.
Article Summary: Xbox is testing free, ad-supported cloud game streaming for insiders. Watch a two-minute ad block, then stream games you own for an hour. Only games you already own, plus free-to-play titles. Xbox console prices go up again on august 1.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
